title: PC completely dead (no lights, no fan spin)
summary: The system receives zero electrical power when pressing the power switch, leaving all LEDs dark and fans motionless.
symptoms: No response when pressing the power button
Motherboard standby LEDs do not illuminate
Power supply fan does not spin

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Verify wall outlet and power strip
fix_steps.detail: Plug a lamp or phone charger into the exact wall outlet to confirm live mains voltage. If using a surge protector, toggle its rocker switch or test directly into the wall.

fix_steps.title: Inspect PSU rocker switch and AC cable
fix_steps.detail: Verify the switch on the back of the power supply unit is flipped to the 'I' (On) position, and firmly push the C13 AC power cord into the power inlet.

fix_steps.title: Perform the paperclip PSU self-test
fix_steps.detail: Disconnect all power cables from PC hardware. Jump the green wire (PS_ON) to any black ground wire on the 24-pin ATX connector with a paperclip. Switch on PSU; if the fan does not spin, the power supply has failed.

fix_steps.title: Test front-panel power switch header
fix_steps.detail: Locate the front-panel header pins (PWR_SW) on the bottom right of the motherboard. Disconnect the case cable and briefly bridge the two pins with a flathead screwdriver to bypass a faulty chassis switch. SAFETY: Bridge ONLY the two PWR_SW pins. Never touch 12V RGB headers, USB headers, or audio pins, as shorting voltage rails will permanently damage the motherboard.

title: Fans spin for a second then immediately shut off
summary: The power supply initiates boot but triggers internal short-circuit protection (SCP/OCP) almost instantly to prevent component damage.
symptoms: Fans spin for half a second before halting
Power LED flashes once then turns off
System requires power cord pull to attempt turning on again

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Check 8-pin CPU (EPS) power cable
fix_steps.detail: Ensure the 8-pin CPU power cable near the top left of the motherboard is fully seated. Do not confuse 8-pin PCIe graphics cables with 8-pin EPS CPU cables.

fix_steps.title: Inspect for motherboard standoff shorts
fix_steps.detail: Ensure only required motherboard standoffs are installed in the chassis. An extra standoff behind the motherboard can short power traces to the case chassis.

fix_steps.title: Strip down to bare minimum components
fix_steps.detail: Disconnect all SATA drives, front USB headers, RGB hubs, and add-in cards. Boot with only CPU, one RAM stick, and motherboard to identify the shorted component.

fix_steps.title: Inspect PCIe auxiliary connectors on the GPU
fix_steps.detail: Look for burnt pins or melted plastic on 12VHPWR or 8-pin PCIe headers, which trigger emergency PSU latch-off.

title: Motherboard powers on but hangs on CPU debug LED
summary: Motherboard LEDs and fans operate, but the Power-On Self-Test fails at processor initialization, leaving a solid red or white CPU diagnostic LED.
symptoms: EZ Debug CPU LED stays illuminated continuously
Monitor stays in sleep mode with no video signal
Fans spin at high speed without throttling down

fix_steps.title: Safety isolation and power discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, switch off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall. Press and hold the chassis power button for 5 seconds while unplugged to drain all residual capacitor energy before touching any internal hardware.

fix_steps.title: Check CPU compatibility and BIOS revision
fix_steps.detail: Modern motherboards often require a BIOS update to support newer processor generations. Use the rear USB Flashback button to flash the latest BIOS without a supported CPU installed. CRITICAL: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard.

fix_steps.title: Reseat processor and inspect socket pins
fix_steps.detail: Remove the CPU cooler and CPU. On Intel LGA or AMD AM5 sockets, inspect pins with bright light and magnifier for bends or socket debris. On AM4, verify no bent pins on the CPU underside.

fix_steps.title: Loosen uneven CPU cooler mounting pressure
fix_steps.detail: Overtightened cooler screws can flex the motherboard substrate and cause pins to lose contact with the memory controller or power delivery contacts.

fix_steps.title: Clear CMOS battery
fix_steps.detail: Unplug wall power, remove the CR2032 coin cell battery for 5 minutes, short the CLR_CMOS jumper, and reinstall to clear corrupted hardware states.

title: Motherboard hangs on DRAM debug LED (no display)
summary: System fails POST during initial memory training, indicated by a yellow or amber DRAM indicator LED and no screen output.
symptoms: DRAM diagnostic LED stays solid amber or yellow
No video output to monitor
Continuous long beeps on motherboards with internal speaker

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Verify primary DIMM slot population (A2 / B2)
fix_steps.detail: Dual-channel motherboards require memory in slots 2 and 4 (counted from CPU socket). Installing in slots 1 and 3 frequently prevents POST.

fix_steps.title: Isolate with a single RAM stick
fix_steps.detail: Remove all memory modules except one placed in slot A2. Power on to test. Swap sticks to identify whether a module or slot is defective.

fix_steps.title: Allow time for DDR5 memory training
fix_steps.detail: On DDR5 platforms (AM5 and LGA 1700), initial boot and BIOS resets require up to 3-5 minutes of silent memory training before video appears. Do not interrupt.

fix_steps.title: Clean gold RAM contacts with isopropyl alcohol
fix_steps.detail: Wipe the gold edge contacts using 90%+ isopropyl alcohol or a clean pencil eraser to eliminate skin oils or oxidation, then seat firmly until both latches click.

title: VGA debug LED lit or 1 long, 3 short beeps
summary: The system passes CPU and memory checks but cannot initialize video output or detect a display adapter.
symptoms: VGA debug LED remains lit white or red
Speaker emits 1 long beep followed by 3 short beeps
Monitor reports 'No Signal' or enters power saving standby

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Verify cable connection to dedicated GPU, not motherboard
fix_steps.detail: Ensure HDMI or DisplayPort cable is plugged directly into the graphics card outputs, not the rear motherboard I/O ports (which require integrated graphics).

fix_steps.title: Reseat GPU into primary PCIe x16 slot
fix_steps.detail: Unlatch the PCIe retention clip, pull the graphics card, clean dust from slot, and push firmly until the retention latch snaps closed.

fix_steps.title: Use separate PCIe power cables
fix_steps.detail: Avoid daisy-chaining a single split cable for high-power cards. Run dedicated individual 8-pin PCIe cables directly from the PSU to each connector.

fix_steps.title: Test with an alternative display cable and port
fix_steps.detail: Swap between DisplayPort and HDMI cables. High-resolution monitors can fail handshake if using an outdated or non-VESA certified cable.

title: System boots to BIOS or hangs on BOOT debug LED
summary: Core hardware initializes successfully, but the motherboard firmware cannot locate an active operating system boot loader.
symptoms: Motherboard BOOT LED stays green/yellow
PC boots straight into BIOS setup screen on every power up
Message: 'Reboot and Select proper Boot device'

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Toggle CSM / UEFI boot mode in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: If Windows was installed in legacy MBR mode, enabling UEFI only will hide the drive. In BIOS Settings, test toggling CSM (Compatibility Support Module) On or Off.

fix_steps.title: Verify NVMe/SATA drive detection in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: Check the NVMe Configuration or Storage Information tab in BIOS. If the SSD is not listed, reseat the M.2 SSD or replace the SATA data cable.

fix_steps.title: Adjust Boot Priority list
fix_steps.detail: Set 'Windows Boot Manager' on your primary OS drive as Boot Option #1 rather than generic drive names or USB storage devices.

fix_steps.title: Repair EFI bootloader with Windows installation media
fix_steps.detail: Boot from a Windows USB installer, select Repair Your Computer → Command Prompt, and run 'bootrec /fixboot' and 'bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI'.

title: PC freezes on motherboard splash screen (spinning dots freeze)
summary: The system completes POST and displays the manufacturer logo, but halts indefinitely during early hardware enumeration.
symptoms: Stuck on ASUS, MSI, Gigabyte, or ASRock logo
Windows spinning loading circle freezes solid
Keyboard Caps Lock LED does not respond to presses

fix_steps.title: Unplug all external USB peripherals
fix_steps.detail: Remove external hard drives, USB audio interfaces, webcams, and flash drives. Faulty USB controllers often block kernel hardware initialization.

fix_steps.title: Disconnect secondary storage drives
fix_steps.detail: A failing secondary HDD or SSD with bad sectors will stall Windows storage enumeration during boot. Disconnect all drives except the primary OS drive.

fix_steps.title: Disable Fast Boot in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: Enter BIOS setup and disable Fast Boot. This forces full hardware re-initialization on startup instead of loading cached hardware states.

fix_steps.title: Check for corrupted BIOS flash
fix_steps.detail: Clear CMOS and restore BIOS defaults (F5 or F7) to discard unstable memory sub-timings or corrupted ACPI tables.

title: Display goes black after Windows loading dots
summary: System finishes UEFI/BIOS handover and starts loading Windows, but cuts video signal the moment the display driver initializes.
symptoms: Windows logo appears then monitor goes completely black
Monitor goes into standby or displays 'Out of Range'
Hard drive activity LED continues flickering in background

fix_steps.title: Boot into Windows Safe Mode
fix_steps.detail: Interrupt boot three times by holding the power button. In Recovery Mode, navigate to Troubleshoot → Advanced Options → Startup Settings → Restart → press 4 for Safe Mode.

fix_steps.title: Uninstall graphics driver via DDU
fix_steps.detail: In Safe Mode, run Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) to wipe Nvidia/AMD/Intel drivers completely, reboot normally, and install the clean WHQL release.

fix_steps.title: Reset video refresh rate and resolution
fix_steps.detail: Press Windows Key + Ctrl + Shift + B to trigger a graphics driver restart chime, or connect to a secondary display or TV to lower refresh rate.

fix_steps.title: Check display adapter output port
fix_steps.detail: Some multi-output GPUs prioritize DisplayPort 1 over HDMI. Connect to a different physical port on the graphics card.

title: BSOD with INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE at startup
summary: Windows kernel loses access to the system partition during early startup due to changed storage controller modes or missing AHCI/NVMe drivers.
symptoms: Blue screen with stop code INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE
Immediate reboot after splash screen into automatic repair
Occurs after BIOS update or motherboard replacement

fix_steps.title: Verify SATA / NVMe mode in BIOS (AHCI vs RAID / VMD)
fix_steps.detail: Enter BIOS and locate SATA Operation or Intel VMD. If a prior firmware update or CMOS reset reverted the storage controller from AHCI to RAID/VMD (or vice versa), switch it back to your original configuration.

fix_steps.title: Boot into Safe Mode once to reload storage drivers
fix_steps.detail: Safe Mode loads generic Microsoft storage drivers. Booting into Safe Mode once often clears driver binding conflicts and allows normal boots thereafter.

fix_steps.title: Run CHKDSK from Windows Recovery Environment
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt from Advanced Startup and run 'chkdsk C: /f /r' to repair corrupted file system structures on the boot partition.

fix_steps.title: Check system file integrity with SFC
fix_steps.detail: In Recovery Command Prompt, run 'sfc /scannow /offbootdir=C:\ /offwindir=C:\Windows' to replace corrupted kernel storage drivers.

title: BOOTMGR is missing (Press Ctrl+Alt+Del to restart)
summary: Legacy BIOS system cannot find the Windows Boot Manager file in the active partition volume boot record.
symptoms: Black screen with white text: 'BOOTMGR is missing'
Pressing Ctrl+Alt+Del loops back to identical error
Occurs after partition resizing or secondary drive installation

fix_steps.title: Check boot device order in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: Ensure BIOS is not trying to boot from a secondary storage HDD, external USB drive, or network PXE boot rather than the primary Windows drive.

fix_steps.title: Rebuild BCD store using Command Prompt
fix_steps.detail: Boot from Windows USB, open Command Prompt, and execute: 'bootrec /fixmbr', 'bootrec /fixboot', and 'bootrec /rebuildbcd'.

fix_steps.title: Mark system partition as active using Diskpart
fix_steps.detail: In Command Prompt, run diskpart → select disk 0 → select partition 1 → active → exit, ensuring BIOS directs to the correct bootable partition.

fix_steps.title: Inspect storage drive health
fix_steps.detail: Corrupted BOOTMGR can indicate failing disk sectors. Connect drive to another PC and check CrystalDiskInfo SMART health.

title: Stuck in 'Preparing Automatic Repair' loop
summary: Windows repeatedly crashes during boot, triggering diagnostic repair which fails and restarts the loop.
symptoms: Screen displays 'Preparing Automatic Repair' followed by 'Diagnosing your PC'
Error: 'Automatic Repair couldn't repair your PC' with SrtTrail.txt log
Selecting Restart loops back to the same repair screen

fix_steps.title: Disable Automatic Startup Repair loop
fix_steps.detail: In Advanced Options → Command Prompt, run: 'bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No' to see the underlying stop code causing crashes.

fix_steps.title: Restore corrupted registry hives
fix_steps.detail: Navigate to 'C:\Windows\System32\config' in Command Prompt. Check if RegBack contains valid registry backups or use System Restore.

fix_steps.title: Uninstall recent Windows quality or feature updates
fix_steps.detail: In Recovery Options, select Troubleshoot → Advanced Options → Uninstall Updates → Uninstall latest quality update.

fix_steps.title: Run DISM and SFC offline repair
fix_steps.detail: Execute 'dism /image:C:\ /cleanup-image /revertpendingactions' to clear hung update installations.

title: PC power cycles infinitely every few seconds
summary: System powers on, spins fans for 3 to 10 seconds, shuts down, and automatically turns back on in an endless loop before video output.
symptoms: Endless loop of turning on and off automatically
No display or BIOS splash screen ever appears
Motherboard debug LEDs cycle through CPU → DRAM then shut off

fix_steps.title: Safety isolation and power discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, switch off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall. Press and hold the chassis power button for 5 seconds while unplugged to drain all residual capacitor energy before touching any internal hardware.

fix_steps.title: Clear CMOS and let memory train
fix_steps.detail: Unplug PSU power, remove CMOS battery for 5 minutes, reseat. On next boot, leave PC untouched for 3 minutes while memory retrains.

fix_steps.title: Reseat RAM and test individual sticks
fix_steps.detail: A failed memory stick or corrupted XMP/EXPO timing profile is the most frequent cause of POST power cycling.

fix_steps.title: Check for shorted front-panel USB ports
fix_steps.detail: Inspect front USB ports with a flashlight. Bent internal pins touching the metal port chassis trigger immediate 5V rail shutdown.

fix_steps.title: Test with an alternative power supply
fix_steps.detail: A failing Power Good (PG) signal from the PSU triggers the motherboard to issue a continuous hardware reset cycle.

title: CMOS Checksum Error (resets settings on every boot)
summary: Motherboard non-volatile memory loses stored configuration and date/time whenever AC wall power is removed.
symptoms: Prompt: 'CMOS checksum error - Defaults loaded' on boot
System clock resets to year 2018 or 2020 every shutdown
Overclock and XMP profiles are forgotten every power cut

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Replace CR2032 3V coin cell battery
fix_steps.detail: Standard motherboard CR2032 lithium batteries last 3-5 years. Replace with a fresh brand-name battery.

fix_steps.title: Check CMOS clear jumper position
fix_steps.detail: Verify the CLR_CMOS jumper cap is not left in the 'Clear' position across pins 2-3 instead of normal pins 1-2.

fix_steps.title: Update to the latest stable BIOS revision
fix_steps.detail: Corrupted EEPROM storage sectors can trigger checksum mismatches; flashing fresh firmware overwrites damaged sectors. CRITICAL SAFETY: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard.

fix_steps.title: Save BIOS settings with F10 before exit
fix_steps.detail: Ensure you explicitly save changes with F10 rather than exiting without saving.

title: Stuck on BitLocker recovery key entry screen
summary: Windows stops boot and requests the 48-digit BitLocker recovery key because hardware integrity or TPM state changed.
symptoms: Blue screen titled 'BitLocker' requesting 48-digit numerical key
Key ID displayed with message: 'Enter the recovery key for this drive'
Occurred following BIOS flash, Secure Boot toggle, or GPU swap

fix_steps.title: Retrieve recovery key from Microsoft Account
fix_steps.detail: From a phone or other device, sign in to 'account.microsoft.com/devices/recoverykey' using the Microsoft account associated with the PC.

fix_steps.title: Restore previous BIOS settings (Secure Boot / TPM)
fix_steps.detail: If the key prompt appeared after entering BIOS, ensure Secure Boot is Enabled and fTPM / PTT is Enabled in UEFI settings.

fix_steps.title: Revert hardware changes temporarily
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC and unplug the AC power cord first. If you changed your GPU, SSD slot, or CPU, put back the original part temporarily to boot into Windows and suspend BitLocker protection.

fix_steps.title: Suspend BitLocker before updating firmware in future
fix_steps.detail: Once in Windows, run 'Suspend-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -RebootCount 1' before running firmware updates.

title: Black screen and no POST following a BIOS update
summary: A failed, interrupted, or corrupt BIOS firmware flash leaves the motherboard unable to execute Power-On Self-Test.
symptoms: PC powers on but displays nothing after a BIOS flash
Fans run continuously with no keyboard or mouse LED activity
Power button does not respond to soft press

fix_steps.title: Safety isolation and power discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, switch off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall. Press and hold the chassis power button for 5 seconds while unplugged to drain all residual capacitor energy before touching any internal hardware.

fix_steps.title: Use Motherboard USB BIOS Flashback
fix_steps.detail: Download manufacturer BIOS on another computer. Rename it according to vendor specifications (e.g., ASUS.CAP, MSI.ROM). Copy to a FAT32 USB drive, insert into dedicated Flashback port, and press button for 3 seconds. CRITICAL: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard.

fix_steps.title: Switch to Dual BIOS backup chip (if equipped)
fix_steps.detail: If your motherboard has a physical BIOS switch on the board, toggle to BIOS_B to boot from the factory backup chip.

fix_steps.title: Perform extended hard CMOS discharge
fix_steps.detail: Disconnect all power cords, remove the CR2032 battery, hold down chassis power button for 60 seconds, and leave disconnected for 30 minutes.

fix_steps.title: Contact manufacturer RMA if board lacks Flashback
fix_steps.detail: If the board lacks hardware BIOS Flashback and the primary EEPROM chip is corrupted, the chip requires an external SPI programmer (CH341A) or board RMA. CRITICAL: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard.

title: Front panel power button broken or disconnected
summary: The chassis momentary power switch is broken, internally shorted, or disconnected from the motherboard front panel pin block.
symptoms: Pressing power button feels spongy or doesn't click
PC turns on when using motherboard onboard start button but not case button
System turns on only when holding button at a specific angle

fix_steps.title: Inspect front panel header cable alignment
fix_steps.detail: Consult motherboard manual for front panel pinout (JFP1). Ensure the 2-pin POWER SW connector is firmly seated on pins 6 and 8.

fix_steps.title: Jump the power pins directly
fix_steps.detail: Carefully touch a flathead metal screwdriver across the two PWR_SW pins. If the system turns on immediately, the case button or wiring is defective. SAFETY: Bridge ONLY the two PWR_SW pins. Never touch 12V RGB headers, USB headers, or audio pins, as shorting voltage rails will permanently damage the motherboard.

fix_steps.title: Swap with Reset Switch as temporary fix
fix_steps.detail: Connect the case's 2-pin RESET SW connector to the PWR_SW header pins. Use the smaller reset button to turn the PC on and off.

fix_steps.title: Install external desktop power switch button
fix_steps.detail: Purchase a standalone $5 desktop power switch cable that routes through a rear PCIe bracket to sit on your desk.

title: CMOS battery dead (BIOS clock and settings reset on every boot)
summary: The CR2032 motherboard coin cell battery is depleted, causing the BIOS to lose time, date, and custom memory XMP/EXPO settings whenever mains AC power is switched off.
symptoms: Windows clock shows 00:00 or incorrect year after turning PC on
Motherboard prompts with 'CMOS Date/Time Not Set' or 'Press F1 to Run Setup'
XMP or EXPO RAM profiles keep disabling themselves
PC requires F1 or F2 keystroke every time power cord is reconnected

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Replace the CR2032 coin cell battery
fix_steps.detail: Power off the PC and unplug the power supply. Locate the silver circular battery on the motherboard, gently push the metal retention clip to eject it, and insert a fresh 3V CR2032 lithium battery with the positive (+) side facing up.

fix_steps.title: Enter BIOS and restore correct system time
fix_steps.detail: Boot into BIOS setup by tapping Del or F2. Navigate to System Information or Main, set current date and UTC time, and enable your RAM XMP or EXPO profile.

fix_steps.title: Verify CMOS clear jumper position
fix_steps.detail: Check the CLRTC / CLR_CMOS header on the motherboard. Ensure no jumper cap is bridging the pins; keeping it shorted will continually wipe BIOS NVRAM on every boot.

fix_steps.title: Save settings and test cold boot
fix_steps.detail: Press F10 to save and exit. Shut down Windows, switch off the power supply rocker switch for 60 seconds, turn it back on, and verify the PC boots straight into Windows without resetting.

title: Secure Boot Violation: Invalid signature detected
summary: The UEFI firmware blocks the operating system bootloader because its digital signature has expired, been revoked in the Secure Boot DBX database, or belongs to an unauthenticated secondary OS.
symptoms: Red or blue banner reading 'Secure Boot Violation: Invalid signature detected'
PC boots straight into BIOS setup instead of Windows
Occurs after installing a Windows update or swapping graphics cards

fix_steps.title: Enter UEFI BIOS and inspect Secure Boot state
fix_steps.detail: Restart and tap Del or F2. Navigate to the Security or Boot tab, open Secure Boot Configuration, and confirm whether OS Type is set to 'Windows UEFI mode' rather than 'Other OS'.

fix_steps.title: Restore factory Secure Boot keys
fix_steps.detail: Select 'Key Management' in the Secure Boot menu and click 'Restore Factory Default Keys' or 'Install Default Secure Boot Keys'. This refreshes the PK, KEK, and DB databases.

fix_steps.title: Temporarily switch Secure Boot to Disabled
fix_steps.detail: If boot continues to fail, change Secure Boot from Enabled to Disabled. Save and restart to verify Windows boots normally. Once in Windows, run Windows Update to download the latest signed bootloader.

fix_steps.title: Update motherboard BIOS firmware
fix_steps.detail: Download the latest BIOS from your motherboard manufacturer website onto a FAT32 USB flash drive. Flash the update to receive updated Microsoft revocation lists and re-enable Secure Boot. CRITICAL SAFETY: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard.

title: NVMe boot drive missing from BIOS priority list after sudden power cut
summary: An abrupt power outage or hard reset causes the NVMe SSD controller to enter a lockup or low-power recovery state, making the drive temporarily vanish from the motherboard UEFI boot menu.
symptoms: PC boots straight into BIOS setup utility
M.2 slot shows 'Not Present' or 'Empty' in storage overview
Error: 'Reboot and Select proper Boot device' appears on screen

fix_steps.title: Perform a full motherboard power drain (capacitive discharge)
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, unplug the AC power cord from the wall, and hold down the front chassis power button for 30 full seconds. Reconnect AC power and turn on the PC.

fix_steps.title: Reseat the M.2 NVMe SSD in its slot
fix_steps.detail: Unscrew the M.2 thermal heatsink, remove the NVMe drive, inspect the gold edge contacts for dust, and firmly insert it at a 30-degree angle before fastening the retention standoff.

fix_steps.title: Check CSM / UEFI boot mode compatibility
fix_steps.detail: In BIOS settings, navigate to Boot > CSM (Compatibility Support Module). If your Windows was installed in pure UEFI mode, ensure CSM is Disabled and Windows Boot Manager is selected as Priority 1.

fix_steps.title: Test NVMe in secondary M.2 slot
fix_steps.detail: If the primary CPU-connected M.2 slot does not register the drive, move the SSD to a chipset-connected M.2 slot on the lower half of the motherboard to isolate a dead lane or controller fault.

title: Power supply surge lockout (clicks once and requires AC unplug to reset)
summary: The power supply internal supervisor IC triggers Over-Current Protection (OCP) or Short-Circuit Protection (SCP) due to an electrical surge or transient spike, latching into a protective shutdown.
symptoms: Audible 'click' sound from the PSU when pressing power button, then silence
Power button does nothing on second press until power cord is disconnected
Occurred following a wall socket surge or nearby lightning strike

fix_steps.title: Discharge power supply internal capacitors
fix_steps.detail: Unplug the AC power cord from the back of the PSU. Switch the rocker to 'I', hold the case power button for 20 seconds, plug directly into an isolated wall socket (bypassing old surge strips), and test.

fix_steps.title: Disconnect all internal power cables except 24-pin and 8-pin EPS
fix_steps.detail: Unplug PCIe power cables from the graphics card and all SATA power cables from hard drives and RGB hubs. If the PC now powers on, one of the disconnected accessories has an electrical dead short.

fix_steps.title: Inspect USB ports for bent metal pins touching ground
fix_steps.detail: Examine every front and rear USB Type-A port with a flashlight. If a metal shield pin is bent inward and touching the center plastic tab, it grounds the 5V rail and trips instant PSU latch-off.

fix_steps.title: Test with known-good power supply unit
fix_steps.detail: If the PSU continues clicking off under zero load, the internal primary capacitor or MOSFET has suffered an electrical breakdown and the power supply must be replaced under warranty.

title: Corrupted BIOS black screen recovery via USB Flashback
summary: A failed BIOS update, interrupted flashing process, or incompatible firmware version has corrupted the motherboard SPI flash memory, leaving the computer unable to execute initial boot code.
symptoms: Black screen with fans spinning indefinitely after flashing BIOS
No display signal, no keyboard capslock LED response
Motherboard debug LED stuck on CPU or BIOS code

fix_steps.title: Format a USB flash drive as MBR FAT32
fix_steps.detail: On a working computer, format a USB 2.0 or 3.0 flash drive (32GB or smaller) using FAT32 with Master Boot Record (MBR) partition scheme.

fix_steps.title: Download firmware and rename file with official renamer
fix_steps.detail: Download the correct motherboard BIOS file from the official manufacturer support page. Run the included renamer tool (e.g. ASUS: 'creative.CAP', MSI: 'MSI.ROM', Gigabyte: 'GIGABYTE.bin') and copy the renamed file to the root of the USB drive. CRITICAL SAFETY: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard.

fix_steps.title: Insert drive into designated BIOS Flashback USB port
fix_steps.detail: Locate the specific rear I/O USB port bordered by a white or grey outline labeled 'BIOS Flashback' or 'Q-Flash Plus'. Insert the USB flash drive. CRITICAL: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard. REQUIREMENT: The USB drive must be formatted as FAT32 (not NTFS or exFAT). 4GB drive or larger recommended.

fix_steps.title: Hold Flashback button until LED starts blinking
fix_steps.detail: With the PSU connected and switched on (PC powered off), hold the Flashback button for 3 seconds until the indicator LED starts flashing. Wait 5-8 minutes until the blinking stops completely before powering on. CRITICAL: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard.

title: TPM configuration change prompt loop at startup
summary: The motherboard firmware detects a new CPU or clear CMOS state, triggering a mandatory security confirmation screen to reset the Trusted Platform Module (fTPM / dTPM).
symptoms: Screen displays 'A configuration change was requested to clear this computer TPM'
Prompts 'Press Y to reset fTPM or Press N to keep previous records'
Keyboard keystroke does not register or screen loops on every reboot

fix_steps.title: Ensure BitLocker recovery key is saved before pressing Y
fix_steps.detail: If Windows BitLocker drive encryption is enabled, clearing TPM will require entering your 48-digit BitLocker recovery key from your Microsoft Account (account.microsoft.com/devices/recoverykey).

fix_steps.title: Connect a basic wired USB keyboard directly to rear I/O
fix_steps.detail: Wireless, Bluetooth, or front-panel USB keyboards frequently fail to initialize at this pre-boot prompt. Plug a standard wired USB keyboard into a top rear USB 2.0 port.

fix_steps.title: Press Y to confirm fTPM reset
fix_steps.detail: Press 'Y' (or 'Z' on German QWERTZ keyboards) to confirm the TPM reset. The motherboard will reboot automatically and initialize the new CPU security state.

fix_steps.title: Update BIOS to resolve AMD fTPM stutter fix
fix_steps.detail: If TPM prompts continue appearing after every reboot, update the motherboard BIOS to AGESA 1.2.0.7 or newer to eliminate the known AMD fTPM NVRAM retention bug. CRITICAL: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard.

title: Uneven CPU cooler mounting pressure causing memory channel loss
summary: Overtightening or unevenly torquing CPU cooler screws bends the LGA socket substrate, causing pin contact loss on delicate DDR5/DDR4 memory controller traces and preventing POST.
symptoms: PC boots with 1 RAM stick in slot B2, but fails to POST with 2 sticks in A2/B2
Motherboard DRAM debug LED illuminates solid amber or red
Occurs immediately after installing a new CPU cooler, AIO pump, or contact frame

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Loosen cooler screws by half a turn
fix_steps.detail: Turn each cooler mount screw counterclockwise by half a turn in a cross pattern (top-left, bottom-right, top-right, bottom-left) to relieve asymmetric PCB flexing.

fix_steps.title: Remove cooler and inspect CPU socket pins
fix_steps.detail: Remove the cooler, lift the socket retention lever, and inspect the motherboard LGA socket (Intel LGA 1700 or AMD AM5) with bright light for any bent or flattened gold pins. SAFETY NOTE: If removing a CPU cooler (especially AMD AM4), warm up the CPU with a brief workload first, then twist the cooler gently left and right before lifting. Never yank straight up, as cold paste can rip the CPU out of the socket and bend pins.

fix_steps.title: Clean CPU contact pads with isopropyl alcohol
fix_steps.detail: Wipe the gold pads on the underside of the processor with 99% isopropyl alcohol and a lint-free wipe to remove thermal paste residue or finger oils.

fix_steps.title: Reinstall cooler using alternating diagonal torque
fix_steps.detail: Place the cooler flat on the IHS and turn each screw only 2 turns at a time in an X-pattern until hand-tight stops naturally without forcing.

title: DisplayPort monitor deep sleep no signal on boot
summary: Modern high-refresh gaming monitors fail to wake from DisplayPort deep sleep power states during PC boot, causing the graphics card to report a VGA error LED due to absent EDID handshake.
symptoms: Motherboard white VGA debug LED stays on
Monitor reports 'No DisplayPort Signal' and enters sleep mode
Signal appears immediately if cable is unplugged and plugged back in

fix_steps.title: Disable Deep Sleep in monitor On-Screen Display (OSD)
fix_steps.detail: Press the physical menu joystick on the back of your monitor, open System or Setup settings, locate 'DisplayPort Deep Sleep' or 'Auto Input Sensing', and toggle it to Disabled / Off.

fix_steps.title: Turn monitor on 5 seconds before powering on PC
fix_steps.detail: Turn on the monitor so its internal scaler is active and broadcasting EDID timing information before the graphics card initializes PCIe video output.

fix_steps.title: Install NVIDIA DisplayPort 1.4 / 1.3 Firmware Update
fix_steps.detail: If using a GeForce GTX 900, 1000, or RTX 2000 series GPU, download the official 'NVIDIA Graphics Firmware Update Tool for DisplayPort 1.3 and 1.4 Displays' to fix UEFI blank screen handshakes.

fix_steps.title: Replace budget cable with VESA-Certified DP 1.4 cable
fix_steps.detail: Non-certified DisplayPort cables frequently have Pin 20 connected, sending back-power into the GPU 3.3V rail. Swap with a VESA-certified cable with Pin 20 disconnected.

title: PC randomly restarts or shuts down during heavy gaming with NO blue screen
summary: Computer instantly goes black and powers off or restarts under heavy graphics load without creating a BSOD minidump.
symptoms: PC instantly turns off as if power plug was pulled during heavy games
No blue screen, no dump file in C:\Windows\Minidump
Event Viewer shows Event ID 41 Kernel-Power (unexpected power loss)

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Use separate PCIe power cables instead of daisy-chained pigtail cables
fix_steps.instruction: Check GPU power connectors. High-power graphics cards (RTX 3080/4080, RX 6800/7900) draw up to 350W+. Never use a single split 'pigtail' cable for two 8-pin ports. Run two or three separate individual cables directly from PSU.
fix_steps.caution: A single PCIe cable is rated for 150W; pulling 300W over one cable trips PSU Over-Current Protection (OCP).
fix_steps.detail: Check GPU power connectors. High-power graphics cards (RTX 3080/4080, RX 6800/7900) draw up to 350W+. Never use a single split 'pigtail' cable for two 8-pin ports. Run two or three separate individual cables directly from PSU.

fix_steps.title: Test GPU power target or undervolt to tame transient spikes
fix_steps.instruction: In MSI Afterburner, reduce 'Power Limit' slider to 85% or apply a gentle undervolt. If the PC stops crashing during benchmarks, your PSU is failing to handle microsecond GPU power spikes.
fix_steps.caution: Temporary diagnostic workaround until a higher quality Tier-A/B power supply is installed.
fix_steps.detail: In MSI Afterburner, reduce 'Power Limit' slider to 85% or apply a gentle undervolt. If the PC stops crashing during benchmarks, your PSU is failing to handle microsecond GPU power spikes.

fix_steps.title: Verify PSU wattage and 12V rail health
fix_steps.instruction: Check your PSU rated wattage against total system draw. Modern GPUs have transient spikes up to 2x TDP lasting 10 milliseconds. Older PSUs shut down immediately to protect components.
fix_steps.caution: Avoid budget unrated power supplies; refer to the Cultists Network PSU Tier List.
fix_steps.detail: Check your PSU rated wattage against total system draw. Modern GPUs have transient spikes up to 2x TDP lasting 10 milliseconds. Older PSUs shut down immediately to protect components.

title: BitLocker blue screen asking for 48-digit recovery key on startup
summary: Computer boots directly to blue BitLocker Recovery screen asking for 48-digit numerical key after BIOS update or hardware change.
symptoms: Blue screen on boot: 'BitLocker - Enter the recovery key for this drive'
Triggered after motherboard BIOS update, TPM toggle, or SSD swap
Windows will not boot to desktop without entering 48-digit key

fix_steps.title: Retrieve recovery key from your Microsoft Account portal
fix_steps.instruction: On your phone or another device, go to 'account.microsoft.com/devices/recoverykey'. Sign in with every Microsoft account ever logged into the PC (including school/work accounts). Locate the matching Key ID.
fix_steps.caution: Check the 'Key ID' displayed on the PC screen to ensure you match the correct recovery key.
fix_steps.detail: On your phone or another device, go to 'account.microsoft.com/devices/recoverykey'. Sign in with every Microsoft account ever logged into the PC (including school/work accounts). Locate the matching Key ID.

fix_steps.title: Revert BIOS TPM / Security settings if key is missing
fix_steps.instruction: If you cannot find the key and this started immediately after a BIOS update: enter BIOS settings. Ensure 'fTPM' / 'Intel PTT' is enabled and 'Secure Boot' mode is set to 'Standard'. Do not clear TPM keys.
fix_steps.caution: Never select 'Clear TPM' in BIOS unless you have your 48-digit key or intend to wipe the drive.
fix_steps.detail: If you cannot find the key and this started immediately after a BIOS update: enter BIOS settings. Ensure 'fTPM' / 'Intel PTT' is enabled and 'Secure Boot' mode is set to 'Standard'. Do not clear TPM keys.

fix_steps.title: Suspend BitLocker before performing future BIOS updates
fix_steps.instruction: Once back in Windows, open Command Prompt (Admin) and run: 'manage-bde -protectors -disable C:'. Run your update, then run 'manage-bde -protectors -enable C:'.
fix_steps.caution: Always back up your 48-digit key to a USB drive or printout.
fix_steps.detail: Once back in Windows, open Command Prompt (Admin) and run: 'manage-bde -protectors -disable C:'. Run your update, then run 'manage-bde -protectors -enable C:'. CRITICAL: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard.

title: Black screen with no display signal after enabling Secure Boot in BIOS
summary: Motherboard fails to output display signal or POST after toggling Secure Boot for Valorant / Windows 11.
symptoms: No display signal immediately after enabling Secure Boot or changing PK keys in BIOS
PC turns on, fans spin, but monitor says 'No Signal'
GPU UEFI GOP driver incompatible with CSM disabled

fix_steps.title: Safety isolation and power discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, switch off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall. Press and hold the chassis power button for 5 seconds while unplugged to drain all residual capacitor energy before touching any internal hardware.

fix_steps.title: Clear CMOS to force motherboard back to default CSM settings
fix_steps.instruction: Turn off power supply and unplug PC power cord. Locate the round silver CR2032 battery on motherboard. Use a flathead screwdriver or fingernail to pop battery out. Wait 5 minutes. Reinsert battery and turn PC on.
fix_steps.caution: This resets all BIOS settings back to factory defaults with display output restored.
fix_steps.detail: Turn off power supply and unplug PC power cord. Locate the round silver CR2032 battery on motherboard. use a non-conductive plastic pry tool or fingernail (or carefully with a flathead screwdriver without scratching motherboard traces) to release the battery retention clip. Wait 5 minutes. Reinsert battery and turn PC on.

fix_steps.title: Update GPU UEFI Firmware / GOP driver
fix_steps.instruction: Older GPUs (Nvidia GTX 900/1000 series) lack modern UEFI GOP firmware and black-screen when CSM is disabled. Download the official 'NVIDIA Graphics Firmware Update Tool for DisplayPort 1.3 and 1.4 Displays' in Windows.
fix_steps.caution: Run the firmware updater before attempting to enable Secure Boot again.
fix_steps.detail: Older GPUs (Nvidia GTX 900/1000 series) lack modern UEFI GOP firmware and black-screen when CSM is disabled. Download the official 'NVIDIA Graphics Firmware Update Tool for DisplayPort 1.3 and 1.4 Displays' in Windows.

fix_steps.title: Convert MBR drive to GPT before disabling CSM
fix_steps.instruction: If your Windows drive is formatted as legacy MBR, disabling CSM makes the drive unbootable. In Windows Command Prompt (Admin), run 'mbr2gpt /validate /allowFullOS' then 'mbr2gpt /convert /allowFullOS'.
fix_steps.caution: Do not convert if you are dual-booting with 32-bit legacy operating systems.
fix_steps.detail: If your Windows drive is formatted as legacy MBR, disabling CSM makes the drive unbootable. In Windows Command Prompt (Admin), run 'mbr2gpt /validate /allowFullOS' then 'mbr2gpt /convert /allowFullOS'.

title: New NVMe M.2 SSD or SATA hard drive not showing up in File Explorer
summary: Installed a new solid-state drive or hard drive but it does not appear in 'This PC' or File Explorer.
symptoms: New SSD installed but missing in File Explorer / 'This PC'
BIOS detects the SSD model name but Windows does not show the drive
Drive is unallocated or missing drive letter

fix_steps.title: Initialize and format disk in Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc)
fix_steps.instruction: Press Win+X, select 'Disk Management' (or press Win+R and type 'diskmgmt.msc'). Look at the bottom list for a disk marked 'Unknown / Not Initialized' or 'Unallocated'.
fix_steps.caution: Make sure you select the brand new unallocated disk, not your existing OS drive.
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+X, select 'Disk Management' (or press Win+R and type 'diskmgmt.msc'). Look at the bottom list for a disk marked 'Unknown / Not Initialized' or 'Unallocated'.

fix_steps.title: Initialize disk as GPT partition style
fix_steps.instruction: Right-click the disk number (e.g. 'Disk 1') -> select 'Initialize Disk'. Choose 'GPT (GUID Partition Table)' -> click OK.
fix_steps.caution: Always choose GPT for modern drives and NVMe SSDs; MBR is legacy only.
fix_steps.detail: Right-click the disk number (e.g. 'Disk 1') -> select 'Initialize Disk'. Choose 'GPT (GUID Partition Table)' -> click OK.

fix_steps.title: Create Simple Volume and assign drive letter
fix_steps.instruction: Right-click the black 'Unallocated' space -> select 'New Simple Volume'. Follow the wizard: assign maximum size, choose a drive letter (e.g. D: or E:), format as NTFS with 'Perform a quick format'. Click Finish.
fix_steps.caution: Your new SSD will now immediately appear in File Explorer ready for use.
fix_steps.detail: Right-click the black 'Unallocated' space -> select 'New Simple Volume'. Follow the wizard: assign maximum size, choose a drive letter (e.g. D: or E:), format as NTFS with 'Perform a quick format'. Click Finish.

title: Laptop burning hot and battery drains while closed inside backpack (Modern Standby)
summary: Laptop wakes up inside laptop sleeve or backpack, fans scream at 100%, and battery is completely drained.
symptoms: Laptop burning hot to the touch when pulled out of bag
Battery drained from 100% to 0% while lid was closed
Windows 11 Modern Standby (S0 low power idle) staying active

fix_steps.title: Switch Windows lid close action to 'Hibernate' instead of 'Sleep'
fix_steps.instruction: Press Win+R, type 'powercfg.cpl' and press Enter. Click 'Choose what closing the lid does' on the left sidebar. Set 'When I close the lid:' to 'Hibernate' for both On Battery and Plugged In.
fix_steps.caution: Hibernate saves complete RAM state to disk and powers off the motherboard 100% with zero heat and zero battery drain.
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+R, type 'powercfg.cpl' and press Enter. Click 'Choose what closing the lid does' on the left sidebar. Set 'When I close the lid:' to 'Hibernate' for both On Battery and Plugged In.

fix_steps.title: Disable Network Connectivity in Standby
fix_steps.instruction: Open Windows Settings -> System -> Power & battery. Under 'Network connectivity in standby', set to 'Never' (or run in Admin terminal: 'powercfg /setdcvalueindex scheme_current sub_none F15ADD7D-0D7D-4863-A7D0-84E73B719971 0').
fix_steps.caution: Prevents Windows from waking up in your bag to download telemetry or email updates.
fix_steps.detail: Open Windows Settings -> System -> Power & battery. Under 'Network connectivity in standby', set to 'Never' (or run in Admin terminal: 'powercfg /setdcvalueindex scheme_current sub_none F15ADD7D-0D7D-4863-A7D0-84E73B719971 0').

fix_steps.title: Check sleep study logs for wake culprits
fix_steps.instruction: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run: 'powercfg /sleepstudy'. Open the generated HTML file in your browser to inspect which USB device, Bluetooth radio, or background app triggered the wake event.
fix_steps.caution: Look for entries with 'Low Power State Time' below 90%.
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run: 'powercfg /sleepstudy'. Open the generated HTML file in your browser to inspect which USB device, Bluetooth radio, or background app triggered the wake event.

title: Breadboarding a PC: Testing core components outside the case on cardboard
summary: Isolate persistent short circuits, motherboard stand-off shorts, and non-POST issues by assembling bare minimum components outside case.
symptoms: PC fails to turn on or clicks off immediately inside case
Motherboard suspected of shorting against metal chassis or standoff
Fans twitch for 1 millisecond and shut down

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Disassemble motherboard and place on non-conductive cardboard box
fix_steps.instruction: Remove motherboard from PC case. Place it on the flat cardboard motherboard box. CRITICAL: Never place it on an anti-static bag (the outer surface of anti-static bags is electrically conductive).
fix_steps.caution: CRITICAL: Anti-static bags are conductive on the outside; only use plain dry cardboard or wood.
fix_steps.detail: Remove motherboard from PC case. Place it on the flat cardboard motherboard box. CRITICAL: Never place it on an anti-static bag (the outer surface of anti-static bags is electrically conductive).

fix_steps.title: Install only the absolute bare minimum components
fix_steps.instruction: Install ONLY: CPU + CPU cooler, 1 stick of RAM in slot 2, 24-pin ATX power cable, and 8-pin EPS CPU power cable. Disconnect all SATA cables, front panel wires, case fans, and RGB headers.
fix_steps.caution: If CPU lacks integrated graphics, install your GPU and connect its PCIe power cables.
fix_steps.detail: Install ONLY: CPU + CPU cooler, 1 stick of RAM in slot 2, 24-pin ATX power cable, and 8-pin EPS CPU power cable. Disconnect all SATA cables, front panel wires, case fans, and RGB headers.

fix_steps.title: Bridge the two Power Switch pins with a flathead screwdriver
fix_steps.instruction: Locate the front panel header (JFP1 / PANEL). Momentarily touch the tip of a metal screwdriver across the two 'PWR_SW' (Power Switch) pins for 1 second to turn on the board.
fix_steps.caution: If the system POSTs cleanly on cardboard, your PC case has an extra standoff shorting the back of the motherboard.
fix_steps.detail: Locate the front panel header (JFP1 / PANEL). Momentarily touch the tip of a metal screwdriver across the two 'PWR_SW' (Power Switch) pins for 1 second to turn on the board. SAFETY: Bridge ONLY the two PWR_SW pins. Never touch 12V RGB headers, USB headers, or audio pins, as shorting voltage rails will permanently damage the motherboard.

title: ASUS Q-LED and Q-Code Motherboard Debug Diagnostic Guide
summary: Diagnose ASUS motherboard POST failures using 4-color Q-LED status lights (CPU, DRAM, VGA, BOOT) and 2-digit alphanumeric Q-Code hexadecimal readouts.
symptoms: System fails to complete POST
Q-LED stays lit on Red (CPU), Yellow (DRAM), White (VGA), or Yellow-Green (BOOT)
2-digit Q-Code LED displays codes 00, 55, d6, or 99

fix_steps.title: Decode Q-LED color indicator
fix_steps.detail: Observe the four color LEDs adjacent to the 24-pin ATX connector. Red indicates CPU failure or missing 8-pin EPS 12V connection; Yellow indicates DRAM memory training failure; White indicates VGA GPU handshake failure; Yellow-Green indicates no bootable OS device found.

fix_steps.title: Decode 2-digit Q-Code readout
fix_steps.detail: If your board includes a 7-segment display, read the hex code. Code 00 indicates CPU not detected or seated incorrectly; Code 55 indicates memory not detected; Code d6 indicates no console output device (GPU); Code 99 indicates Super I/O or PCIe initialization halt.

fix_steps.title: Clear CMOS and reset memory profiles
fix_steps.detail: Shut down PC, unplug AC power cord, and press the Clear CMOS rear I/O button for 5 seconds (or bridge the 2-pin CLRTC header with a screwdriver) to wipe unstable DOCP, EXPO, or memory timings.

fix_steps.title: Isolate memory to slot A2
fix_steps.detail: Remove all RAM sticks except a single module in primary DIMM slot A2 (second slot away from CPU). Power on and allow up to 3 minutes for initial DDR5 memory training to complete.

title: MSI EZ Debug LED Motherboard Diagnostic and POST Triage
summary: Troubleshoot boot hangs and hardware initialization failures indicated by MSI EZ Debug LEDs (CPU, DRAM, VGA, BOOT) and 2-digit Debug Code LEDs.
symptoms: MSI motherboard stops during power-on sequence
One of four EZ Debug LEDs remains constantly illuminated
Black screen with case fans spinning at high speed

fix_steps.title: Safety isolation and power discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, switch off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall. Press and hold the chassis power button for 5 seconds while unplugged to drain all residual capacitor energy before touching any internal hardware.

fix_steps.title: Inspect EZ Debug LED sequence
fix_steps.detail: During normal boot, MSI boards cycle through CPU -> DRAM -> VGA -> BOOT and turn off. If an LED halts and remains solidly lit, initialization failed on that specific component.

fix_steps.title: Resolve DRAM LED hang
fix_steps.detail: Turn off power and reseat RAM sticks firmly into slots DIMMA2 and DIMMB2 until both retention clips click. Test with a single stick in DIMMA2 if dual-channel training fails.

fix_steps.title: Resolve CPU LED hang
fix_steps.detail: Verify the EPS 8-pin CPU power cable is firmly clicked into the top-left motherboard header (do not confuse with PCIe 8-pin). Check CPU socket for bent pins or uneven cooler mounting pressure.

fix_steps.title: Resolve VGA LED hang
fix_steps.detail: Reseat the graphics card into the primary PCIe x16 slot. Ensure all 8-pin or 12VHPWR auxiliary power cables are fully locked with zero gap.

title: Gigabyte Motherboard Status Code Display and Debug LED Triage
summary: Diagnose Gigabyte AORUS motherboard boot failures using onboard 2-digit 7-segment status codes and 4-phase diagnostic LEDs.
symptoms: Motherboard hangs on 2-digit code such as C1, 54, 78, or 90
Diagnostic status LED stays illuminated without video display
Monitor displays no signal while fans spin continuously

fix_steps.title: Safety isolation and power discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, switch off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall. Press and hold the chassis power button for 5 seconds while unplugged to drain all residual capacitor energy before touching any internal hardware.

fix_steps.title: Read 7-segment debug display code
fix_steps.detail: Inspect the 2-digit LED readout at the bottom or top edge of the motherboard. Identify whether the system is stuck in an initialization loop or halting on a specific subsystem code.

fix_steps.title: Diagnose memory training codes (C1, 54, 15)
fix_steps.detail: Codes 15, C1, and 54 indicate DRAM memory training. On AMD AM5 and Intel LGA1700 platforms, first-time memory training can take 2 to 4 minutes. If it exceeds 5 minutes, clear CMOS and test single stick in DDR5_A2.

fix_steps.title: Inspect PCIe lane initialization (Codes d6, 78)
fix_steps.detail: Code d6 or 78 indicates GPU display handshake failure. Ensure monitor cable is plugged into GPU rather than motherboard I/O panel. Reseat graphics card and check monitor input source. Always release the plastic PCIe retention lock at the end of the slot before pulling the graphics card to avoid tearing the slot off the motherboard.

fix_steps.title: Flash BIOS using Q-Flash Plus
fix_steps.detail: If CPU is newer than factory BIOS, use Gigabyte Q-Flash Plus button: format USB drive to FAT32, rename BIOS file to GIGABYTE.bin, insert into designated Q-Flash USB port, and press button with PC in standby. CRITICAL: Never turn off, reset, or unplug the PC while the BIOS update is flashing. A power interruption during EEPROM write will corrupt the firmware and brick the motherboard.

title: ASRock Dr. Debug Hexadecimal POST Code Triage
summary: Decode ASRock Dr. Debug 2-digit hexadecimal POST codes to isolate CPU, memory, chipset, and GPU hardware initialization failures.
symptoms: ASRock motherboard stops booting with 2-digit LED code displayed
POST stops at code 00, 19, 4C, 53, or d7
System powers on but fails to enter BIOS setup screen

fix_steps.title: Reference Dr. Debug code table
fix_steps.detail: Code 00 means CPU not detected; Code 19 indicates early Southbridge/chipset initialization; Code 4C/53 indicates memory detection and training error; Code d7 indicates console input device (keyboard/mouse) not detected.

fix_steps.title: Perform power cycle and clear CMOS
fix_steps.detail: Power off system, unplug AC power cord, and short the CLRCMOS1 jumper pins for 10 seconds (or press the rear Clear CMOS button) to reset BIOS settings.

fix_steps.title: Reseat DIMM modules in slots A2 and B2
fix_steps.detail: ASRock motherboards require memory installed in slots DDR4_A2 and DDR4_B2 (or DDR5_A2 and DDR5_B2). Clean DIMM edge contacts with isopropyl alcohol before reseating. Press firmly on both ends until the retention latches snap shut with an audible click.

fix_steps.title: Disconnect peripheral devices
fix_steps.detail: Unplug all external USB drives, hubs, webcams, and RGB controllers. A failing USB peripheral frequently halts Dr. Debug at codes b4 or d7 during device enumeration.

title: Motherboard POST Beep Codes Diagnostic Guide (AMI, Award, Phoenix)
summary: Interpret standard motherboard speaker acoustic beep codes across American Megatrends (AMI) and Award BIOS architectures to identify hardware faults.
symptoms: Internal motherboard PC speaker emits beeping patterns upon power on
Screen remains completely black without video output
System fails to complete Power-On Self Test

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Connect internal PC buzzer or speaker
fix_steps.detail: Verify a 4-pin piezo buzzer is connected to the SPEAKER pins on the front panel header. Modern cases lack built-in speakers, requiring a standalone buzzer to hear acoustic error codes.

fix_steps.title: Decode AMI BIOS beep codes
fix_steps.detail: 1 short beep indicates successful POST; 1 continuous long beep indicates memory refresh failure; 5 short beeps indicate CPU failure; 1 long 3 short beeps indicate memory test failure; 1 long 8 short beeps indicate video adapter failure.

fix_steps.title: Decode Award BIOS beep codes
fix_steps.detail: 1 long 2 short beeps indicate video adapter error or loose GPU; 1 long 3 short beeps indicate keyboard controller failure; continuous repeating high-pitched beeps indicate memory error or overheating.

fix_steps.title: Test minimum configuration
fix_steps.detail: Disconnect all storage drives, remove GPU (if CPU has integrated graphics), and test with one RAM stick to isolate which component triggers the fault beep.

title: Dell and HP Power Button Diagnostic Blink Code Triage
summary: Decode OEM prebuilt desktop and laptop power button amber and white flashing LED patterns to troubleshoot hardware startup failures.
symptoms: Power button flashes repeatedly in amber and white blink sequences
Fans pulse briefly but screen remains black
System will not boot or display manufacturer splash logo

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Count Dell power button blink sequence
fix_steps.detail: Dell diagnostic codes flash amber followed by white. For example: 2 amber, 1 white indicates CPU failure; 2 amber, 3 white indicates system board/memory failure; 2 amber, 7 white indicates LCD/display failure; 3 amber, 3 white indicates BIOS recovery image missing.

fix_steps.title: Count HP power and Caps Lock blink sequence
fix_steps.detail: HP systems blink the Caps Lock LED and power button. For example: 3 slow blinks followed by 2 fast blinks indicates memory module failure; 5 slow blinks followed by 2 fast blinks indicates embedded controller timeout or system board fault.

fix_steps.title: Perform hard RTC real-time clock reset
fix_steps.detail: Disconnect AC power cord, remove laptop battery if external, and hold the power button down for a full 30 to 35 seconds to force a hardware RTC reset and clear corrupted CMOS registers.

fix_steps.title: Reseat memory and clean contacts
fix_steps.detail: Open chassis or service hatch, remove RAM modules, clean gold contacts with a lint-free swab dampened with 99% isopropyl alcohol, and reseat firmly in primary slots. Press firmly on both ends until the retention latches snap shut with an audible click.

title: ATX 24-Pin Power Sequence and PS_ON Green Wire Triage
summary: Test ATX power supply startup sequences using the paperclip green wire PS_ON jump test and verify primary +12V, +5V, and +3.3V DC rail delivery.
symptoms: PC does not respond at all when pressing the front power button
Zero lights, zero fan movement, and zero acoustic clicks from PSU
Suspected dead power supply, blown fuse, or broken front panel switch

fix_steps.title: Disconnect power and unplug 24-pin connector
fix_steps.detail: Turn off the PSU rocker switch and unplug the AC wall cable. Unplug the 24-pin main motherboard power connector and all internal power cables.

fix_steps.title: Perform paperclip PS_ON jump test
fix_steps.detail: Locate Pin 16 PS_ON# (green wire on standard ATX cables) and any adjacent COM ground pin (black wire, Pins 15, 17, or 18). Bend a metal paperclip and insert ends into Pin 16 and Pin 17.

fix_steps.title: Connect minimum load and power on
fix_steps.detail: Connect a single 12V case fan or old SATA drive to provide minimum load. Plug AC cord in and flip rocker switch to ON. If PSU fan spins, the power supply turns on correctly.

fix_steps.title: Measure DC rail voltages with multimeter
fix_steps.detail: Using a digital multimeter, check yellow wires for +12V DC, red wires for +5V DC, orange wires for +3.3V DC, and purple wire for +5VSB standby voltage. Replace PSU if voltages fall below 5% tolerance.

title: PSU Power Good PWR_OK Signal Delay and 5VSB Standby Rail Timing
summary: Diagnose power supply startup handshake failures where +5VSB standby power is present but the PWR_OK (Power Good) signal fails to assert within 100-500ms.
symptoms: Motherboard standby RGB lights illuminate but pressing power button produces an audible click and zero fan movement
PC fan twitches for a fraction of a second then immediately shuts off
System refuses to enter S0 running power state

fix_steps.title: Safety power-off and discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down the PC, turn off the power supply rocker switch (O), and unplug the AC power cord from the wall outlet. Press the front power button once while unplugged to discharge residual capacitor energy before touching any internal components.

fix_steps.title: Verify Pin 9 (+5VSB purple wire) standby voltage
fix_steps.detail: With PSU plugged in and rocker switch on, test Pin 9 against ground with a multimeter. It must read between +4.75V and +5.25V DC. If absent or below 4.5V, the standby transformer is dead.

fix_steps.title: Measure Pin 8 (PWR_OK / Power Good gray wire) signal
fix_steps.detail: The PWR_OK signal informs the motherboard chipset that all DC voltages have stabilized. ATX specification requires PWR_OK to rise to +5V within 100ms to 500ms after PS_ON# assertion. A delay outside this window causes the motherboard to abort startup.

fix_steps.title: Isolate 12V rail short circuits
fix_steps.detail: Unplug the 8-pin EPS CPU power cable and all PCIe GPU power cables. If the system turns on without them, a shorted MOSFET on the motherboard VRM or GPU core is triggering PSU protection.

fix_steps.title: Replace failing power supply unit
fix_steps.detail: Degraded capacitors on secondary filtering stages often delay PWR_OK beyond the motherboard 500ms timeout window. Replace unit with a tier-A or tier-B rated power supply.

title: Intel VMD and RST Storage Controller Missing Driver Windows Setup Fix
summary: Resolve missing NVMe drives during Windows 10/11 installation on Intel 11th through 14th Gen systems caused by Intel Volume Management Device (VMD).
symptoms: Windows Setup displays message: We could not find any drives. To get a storage driver, click Load driver
NVMe SSD is fully visible in motherboard BIOS but missing from Windows partition screen
Cannot install Windows on new Intel Core laptop or desktop

fix_steps.title: Download Intel RST VMD driver package
fix_steps.detail: On another computer, visit laptop or motherboard manufacturer support page and download Intel Rapid Storage Technology (IRST) driver package containing VMD storage controller drivers.

fix_steps.title: Extract driver INF files to USB
fix_steps.detail: Open command prompt or 7-Zip to extract the setup executable. Locate the driver folder (named f6vmdflpy-x64 or similar) containing iaStorVD.inf, iaStorVD.sys, and iaStorVD.cat files. Copy folder onto Windows USB install drive.

fix_steps.title: Load driver during Windows Setup
fix_steps.detail: On the Windows Setup disk selection screen, click Load driver, click Browse, navigate to the extracted driver folder on the USB drive, and select Intel RST VMD Controller. Click Next.

fix_steps.title: Alternative: Disable Intel VMD in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: If not using RAID, enter BIOS setup, locate VMD Setup Menu under Advanced or System Configuration, set Intel VMD Controller to Disabled, save changes (F10), and restart Windows Setup.

title: UEFI GPT vs Legacy CSM MBR Partition Table Boot Mode Mismatch
summary: Fix boot failure where BIOS cannot detect a bootable drive due to mismatch between UEFI pure mode (requiring GPT) and Legacy CSM mode (requiring MBR).
symptoms: BIOS boot menu reports: No bootable device found
Storage drive appears in BIOS hardware list but not in boot priority list
PC repeatedly drops directly into BIOS setup after disabling CSM or enabling Secure Boot

fix_steps.title: Check disk partition table style in WinRE
fix_steps.detail: Boot from Windows install media, press Shift+F10 to open command prompt, type diskpart, then list disk. If an asterisk (*) appears in the GPT column for your disk, it is GPT; if blank, it is MBR.

fix_steps.title: Enable CSM in BIOS for MBR disks
fix_steps.detail: If your drive uses MBR partition table, enter BIOS setup, find Compatibility Support Module (CSM), set to Enabled, and set Boot Device Control to UEFI and Legacy OPROM.

fix_steps.title: Convert MBR disk to GPT without data loss
fix_steps.detail: In Windows Recovery command prompt, run: mbr2gpt /validate /disk:0 /allowFullOS. If validation succeeds, run: mbr2gpt /convert /disk:0 /allowFullOS. This creates an EFI system partition and converts partition table to GPT.

fix_steps.title: Switch BIOS to pure UEFI mode
fix_steps.detail: After successful conversion, re-enter BIOS, disable CSM, enable UEFI boot mode and Secure Boot, select Windows Boot Manager as primary boot device, and reboot.

title: EFI System Partition Corrupted BCD Rebuild Procedure
summary: Repair corrupted or missing Boot Configuration Data (BCD) on the UEFI EFI System Partition using Diskpart and the bcdboot command in Windows Recovery.
symptoms: Windows fails to start with error code 0xc000000f, 0xc0000034, or 0xc0000098
Screen displays: The Boot Configuration Data for your PC is missing or contains errors
Automatic Startup Repair fails repeatedly with SrtTrail.txt log error

fix_steps.title: Open Command Prompt in Windows Recovery Environment
fix_steps.detail: Boot from Windows USB installation media, select Next -> Repair your computer -> Troubleshoot -> Advanced options -> Command Prompt.

fix_steps.title: Identify EFI FAT32 system partition with Diskpart
fix_steps.detail: Run diskpart, then list volume. Identify the small FAT32 volume (typically 100MB to 260MB in size). Run select volume X (replace X with EFI volume number), then assign letter=S: to mount it.

fix_steps.title: Format corrupted EFI partition
fix_steps.detail: If the partition file structure is damaged, format it cleanly in diskpart: format fs=fat32 quick label="ESP". Type exit to return to command prompt. DATA SAFETY: Triple-check that you selected the small EFI partition (100MB to 260MB FAT32) and NEVER your main Windows C: drive or data volume, as formatting will permanently erase all data on the selected volume.

fix_steps.title: Rebuild BCD store using bcdboot
fix_steps.detail: Execute command: bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI. If your Windows installation resides on another drive letter, substitute C: with that letter. Verify output: Boot files successfully created.
